title: Evidence added to a verified or pushed card reaches Jira without verify
body:
## Summary
A re-propose that adds new evidence to a `verified` or `pushed` card appends the evidence but leaves the status alone, so `verify` never checks the new quotes, yet `outbox` sends them.

## Description
`propose` handles an existing fp outside snoozed/rejected/dropped by appending evidence and returning `evidence-grew` with the status unchanged (skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:254, skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:270). `verify` only walks `candidate` cards (skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:374, skill/scripts/lib/verify.mjs:201). `outbox` selects every `verified` card and every `pushed` card whose evidence seq grew since the last push (skill/scripts/lib/sync.mjs:141-147) and sends all stored evidence. So a quote that is not in the file is shown in the Jira inbox as if verified. D8 (detection and verification are separate, docs/data-model.md:269) does not hold for these cards.

## Flow
- run 1: propose card with a real quote, verify -> verified
- run 2: same fp, plus a fabricated quote -> `evidence-grew`, status verified
- verify run 2 checks 0 cards
- outbox sends both quotes

## Expected impact
Every card the inbox shows carries only quotes that verify found at the run's head. Fix options: move a verified/pushed card with a new code/doc key back through a check (verify the new keys only, in `verify --run`, by selecting cards whose asserted keys are newer than their last verify transition), or hold the new keys out of the outbox until checked.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no unverified quote reaches the inbox
Before: probe sent ['# Dowser data model', 'THIS LINE DOES NOT EXIST ANYWHERE'] for a verified card; verify checked 0 cards
After: the fabricated quote would be dropped or held back (simulation of the fix: verify selecting grown verified/pushed cards would run findQuote and fail it with quote-not-found)
Method: probe - a scratch script outside the repo drove openStore(':memory:'), propose, verifyRun, outbox against the real lib; the fix itself was not built (ideas-only)
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:269-270 `if (status === 'candidate') refreshCard();\n    return ... clean({ result: added > 0 ? 'evidence-grew' : 'duplicate', fp, added, status, note })`; skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:374 `SELECT fp FROM proposals WHERE last_run_id = ? AND status = 'candidate'`; skill/scripts/lib/sync.mjs:141 `SELECT fp, status FROM proposals WHERE status IN ('verified', 'pushed')`. Probe output: `{ result: 'evidence-grew', status: 'verified' }`, `verify2 checked 0`, outbox `[ 'verified', [ '# Dowser data model', 'THIS LINE DOES NOT EXIST ANYWHERE' ] ]`
impact_why: Unchecked quotes in the inbox break the core promise that every card's evidence was mechanically verified

title: Edge kinds are a hand-typed CHECK, and INSERT OR IGNORE hides a mismatch
body:
## Summary
The `edges.kind` CHECK list is typed by hand in the DDL instead of coming from `EDGE_KINDS`, it is not in the CHECK reconcile set, and `link` uses `INSERT OR IGNORE`, which in SQLite also swallows CHECK violations. A kind added to `EDGE_KINDS` alone would make `link` report `exists` and store nothing.

## Description
`EDGE_KINDS` lives in skill/scripts/lib/edges.mjs:13. The DDL repeats it as literals at skill/scripts/lib/store-core.mjs:104. `CHECKED` (skill/scripts/lib/store-core.mjs:34-39) lists only runs, proposals and evidence, so `reconcileChecks` never widens `edges`, despite the header claim that the SQL can never be a hand-typed copy (skill/scripts/lib/store-core.mjs:19-20). `link` inserts with `INSERT OR IGNORE` and maps `changes == 0` to `exists` (skill/scripts/lib/edges.mjs:27-29). The edges test pins `EDGE_KINDS` to a literal (skill/scripts/tests/edges.test.mjs:24) rather than to the DDL, so it cannot catch the drift. `deliveries.state` (skill/scripts/lib/store-core.mjs:84) is the same pattern.

## Flow
- someone adds `blocks` to EDGE_KINDS
- link validates against EDGE_KINDS: passes
- INSERT OR IGNORE hits the CHECK: row skipped, changes 0
- link returns {result: 'exists'}; nothing stored

## Expected impact
Edge kinds come from one list: generate the CHECK from `EDGE_KINDS` (add it to ENUMS/CHECKED so old stores widen), and use `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (from_fp, to_fp, kind) DO NOTHING` so only the uniqueness conflict is ignored.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a kind mismatch fails loudly instead of being reported as an existing edge
Before: the exact link statement with kind 'blocks' on a fresh store -> changes 0, rows 0, no error
After: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING raises 'CHECK constraint failed' for the same row (SQLite semantics: an upsert clause covers only the named uniqueness constraint)
Method: probe - scratch script ran edges.mjs's INSERT OR IGNORE against a real store; the After is simulation (not built)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/scripts/lib/store-core.mjs:104 `kind      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('unblocks','duplicate-of','follow-up-of','conflicts-with','related')),`; skill/scripts/lib/edges.mjs:27 `const r = db.prepare('INSERT OR IGNORE INTO edges (from_fp, to_fp, kind, by, at, note) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)')`; skill/scripts/lib/edges.mjs:29 `return { result: Number(r.changes) > 0 ? 'linked' : 'exists', from, to, kind };`; probe: `changes 0 rows 0`
impact_why: Latent: today the lists match; the next edge kind would silently lose every link of that kind

title: parseRef reads #L10nProvider as line 10; normalizeAnchor keeps it a symbol
body:
## Summary
The two ref parsers in fingerprint.mjs disagree on symbols that start with `L` and a digit. `normalizeAnchor` only treats a full `L12`, `L12C3`, `L12-L20` fragment as a line; `parseRef` takes any fragment starting `L<digits>` as a line hint.

## Description
`LINE_FRAGMENT` is anchored at both ends (skill/scripts/lib/fingerprint.mjs:29). `parseRef` uses `frag.match(/^L(\d+)/)` with no end anchor (skill/scripts/lib/fingerprint.mjs:100). So `src/i18n.js#L10nProvider` is the anchor `src/i18n.js#L10nProvider` but the evidence ref gets `line: 10`. verify then reports `claimed_line`/`drift` against a line the agent never claimed (skill/scripts/lib/verify.mjs:126-129), and a symbol ref can come out `in-file` instead of a clean in-file match without hint.

## Flow
- evidence ref `src/cache.js#L2Cache` -> parseRef line 2
- quote found on line 140 -> `in-file`, claimed_line 2, drift 138

## Expected impact
One rule: parseRef uses the same anchored `LINE_FRAGMENT` test (and its first number) before reading a line from a fragment.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a symbol ref never produces a phantom line hint
Before: parseRef('src/i18n.js#L10nProvider') -> {path, line: 10}; parseRef('src/cache.js#L2Cache') -> line 2
After: with the anchored test both return {path} only; `#L12` and `#L12-L20` still give 12 (simulation of three cases against the regexes)
Method: probe - scratch script called the real normalizeAnchor and parseRef
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: probe: `src/i18n.js#L10nProvider | anchor: src/i18n.js#L10nProvider | parseRef: {"path":"src/i18n.js","line":10}`; `src/cache.js#L2Cache | anchor: src/cache.js#L2Cache | parseRef: {"path":"src/cache.js","line":2}`; skill/scripts/lib/fingerprint.mjs:29 `const LINE_FRAGMENT = /^L\d+(?:C\d+)?(?:-L?\d+(?:C\d+)?)?$/;`; skill/scripts/lib/fingerprint.mjs:100 `const lf = frag.match(/^L(\d+)/) ?? frag.match(tail);`
impact_why: Misleading drift and claimed_line on symbol refs such as L10n or L2 cache names; verification outcome rarely changes

title: data-model.md still says user_version 6; the store is at 8
body:
## Summary
The data model doc names `PRAGMA user_version = 6`, an upgrade chain ending at 6, and refuses "any version other than 0..6", while the code is at 8 (v7 deliveries, v8 edges, which the same paragraph mentions).

## Description
docs/data-model.md:20 says `PRAGMA user_version = 6`. docs/data-model.md:35-36 says the upgrade runs 1 -> ... -> 6 and that any version other than 0..6 is refused with exit 3. docs/data-model.md:46 says a CHECK widening keeps `user_version` at 6. The code: `USER_VERSION = 8` (skill/scripts/lib/store-core.mjs:14), migrations 6 -> 7 and 7 -> 8 (skill/scripts/lib/store-core.mjs:342-351), and a file at 7 is upgraded, not refused. docs/data-model.md:31 does mention v7/v8, so the paragraph contradicts itself. Also `openStore`'s JSDoc says only "An older known version (v1) is upgraded" (skill/scripts/lib/store-core.mjs:396).

## Flow
- reader checks which store versions an old Dowser can open
- doc says 6 is current; a v8 file would look "newer" than documented

## Expected impact
The doc states 8, the chain 1 -> ... -> 8, and the refusal rule for anything else; the version facts appear once.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the doc matches USER_VERSION
Before: 3 lines say 6, code says 8
After: 0 lines disagree (grep for `user_version` in docs/data-model.md would show 8 only)
Method: simulation - doc edit not made (ideas-only); grep and re-read confirmed the mismatch
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: docs/data-model.md:20 `...with WAL and \`PRAGMA user_version = 6\`...`; docs/data-model.md:35-36 `An existing file is upgraded one step at a time (1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6) and no row is rewritten. Any version other than 0 (new), 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 is refused with exit 3.`; docs/data-model.md:46 `so \`user_version\` stays 6`; skill/scripts/lib/store-core.mjs:14 `export const USER_VERSION = 8;`
impact_why: The store contract doc misstates the version an older Dowser must refuse

title: Verify doc says working tree; code reads the run's head commit
body:
## Summary
The Verify (D8) section of the data model says quotes are matched against the current working tree and that git/sarif evidence is merely passed through. The code reads the file at the run's head commit, fails a quote found only in the working tree as `uncommitted`, and drops a card whose evidence is only git/sarif with `no-checkable-evidence`.

## Description
docs/data-model.md:273-275: "must be a whitespace-normalized substring of the file at the ref's path in the current working tree". Code: skill/scripts/lib/verify.mjs:4-6 and skill/scripts/lib/verify.mjs:80-84 read `fileAt(root, rev, ...)` and return `why: 'uncommitted'`. docs/data-model.md:290 says git and sarif are passed through as unchecked; skill/scripts/lib/verify.mjs:224 drops a card with only those. The status diagram's dropped notes (docs/data-model.md:192) lists only verify-failed and ref-not-ingested.

## Flow
- agent edits a file, cites the uncommitted line
- doc promises a working-tree match; verify drops it as uncommitted

## Expected impact
The doc names the head-commit rule, the `uncommitted` reason and the `no-checkable-evidence` drop, so an agent or reviewer can predict a drop.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - doc matches verify's behaviour
Before: 3 stated rules differ from code
After: 0 (doc edit, simulated)
Method: simulation - re-read both; not edited (ideas-only)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: docs/data-model.md:274-275 `such \`code\`/\`doc\` quote must be a whitespace-normalized substring of the file at the ref's path in the current working tree.`; docs/data-model.md:290 `Only \`git\` and \`sarif\` evidence is passed through as \`unchecked\`. The agent judges it.`; skill/scripts/lib/verify.mjs:84 `return inWorkingTree().found ? { found: false, why: 'uncommitted' } : f;`; skill/scripts/lib/verify.mjs:224 `if (!note && checks.length === 0 && sources.length === 0) note = 'no-checkable-evidence';`
impact_why: Agents following the doc cite uncommitted lines or git-only evidence and get drops the doc does not explain

title: A hydrated card that wakes from snooze can never be pushed
body:
## Summary
`hydrate` writes `provenance.hydrated_from` into the stored provenance. That key is not part of the record: the model's validator and the schema both refuse unknown provenance keys. When a hydrated snoozed card wakes (`snoozed -> verified`), `outbox` sends it with that key and Forge's `checkRecord` refuses it, every push, forever.

## Description
skill/scripts/lib/hydrate.mjs:94 stores `{ ...it.provenance, hydrated_from: 'dowser_memory_pull' }`. validateCandidate refuses unknown provenance keys (skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:473-474); the schema's provenance is `additionalProperties: false` (skill/schema/dowser-proposal-2.schema.json, $defs.provenance). Forge runs `validateCandidate(cand, { wire: true })` on each pushed record (forge/src/core/push.mjs:119). `wakeSnoozed` moves the card to verified without refreshing provenance (skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:42-50); only a resurface to candidate re-writes it (skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:266).

## Flow
- teammate hydrates; an item snoozed in Jira with a past date comes in
- next run start wakes it -> verified
- outbox includes it with provenance.hydrated_from
- Forge: invalid record: provenance:unknown field hydrated_from; it stays verified and is re-sent each outbox

## Expected impact
Hydrated cards push like any other: keep the marker outside the record (e.g. the hydrate run id is already `first_run_id`, harness `dowser-hydrate`), or strip it in `proposalRecord`.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a woken hydrated card is accepted by the push validator
Before: probe -> `forge wire validation: { ok: false, why: 'provenance:unknown field hydrated_from' }`
After: without the key the same record validates (simulation: the remaining provenance {lens_version:'1'} passes model.mjs:471-481)
Method: probe - scratch script ran hydrate, runStart (woke the card), outbox and validateCandidate wire on the real libs
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/scripts/lib/hydrate.mjs:94 `provenance_json: JSON.stringify({ ...it.provenance, hydrated_from: 'dowser_memory_pull' }),`; skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:473-474 `const pvx = extraKey(pv, ['lens_version', 'model', 'harness', 'run_id', 'focus']);\n  if (pvx) return no(\`provenance:unknown field ${pvx}\`);`; forge/src/core/push.mjs:119 `const v = validateCandidate(cand, { wire: true });`; probe: `woke [ '2fbea79e5b6e8dc7' ]`, `provenance { lens_version: '1', hydrated_from: 'dowser_memory_pull' }`, `forge wire validation: { ok: false, why: 'provenance:unknown field hydrated_from' }`
impact_why: Every hydrated snooze that wakes is stuck: refused by Forge on each push, never back in the inbox

title: An ssh remote with a port gives a different project key than https
body:
## Summary
`normalizeRemote` keeps an ssh port in the project key, so `ssh://git@host:2222/Org/Repo.git` and `https://host/Org/Repo.git` land in two stores and send two `project_key`s to Forge. Its twin `webUrl` in git.mjs already strips the ssh port for the same reason.

## Description
skill/scripts/lib/paths.mjs:76-78 keeps `host:port`. skill/scripts/lib/git.mjs:132 drops an ssh port ("an ssh port is not the web port"). The project key names the local store (skill/scripts/lib/paths.mjs:102) and is the `project_key` every Forge tool call carries (outbox, reflect export). Teammates cloning the same repo over ssh-with-port vs https would not share inbox memory or hydrate each other's decisions. Path case is kept too (`Org/Repo` vs `org/repo`), which docs/data-model.md:12-14 states as intended, so it is not part of this finding.

## Flow
- dev A: origin https://gitlab.acme.com/Org/Repo.git -> gitlab-acme-com-Org-Repo
- dev B: origin ssh://git@gitlab.acme.com:2222/Org/Repo.git -> gitlab-acme-com-2222-Org-Repo
- two Forge projects for one repo

## Expected impact
One repo, one key: drop the port for ssh-family schemes as webUrl does (keep it for http(s), where it is part of the address). Existing keys with a port need a one-time alias or migration note (gate: contract).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one repo maps to one project key across clone URLs
Before: probe gives gitlab-acme-com-Org-Repo vs gitlab-acme-com-2222-Org-Repo, while webUrl gives https://gitlab.acme.com/Org/Repo for both
After: both would give gitlab-acme-com-Org-Repo (simulation)
Method: probe - scratch script called the real normalizeRemote and webUrl
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: probe: `https://gitlab.acme.com/Org/Repo.git  gitlab-acme-com-Org-Repo  https://gitlab.acme.com/Org/Repo`; `ssh://git@gitlab.acme.com:2222/Org/Repo.git  gitlab-acme-com-2222-Org-Repo  https://gitlab.acme.com/Org/Repo`; skill/scripts/lib/paths.mjs:78 `if (m) { host = m[2] ? \`${m[1]}:${m[2]}\` : m[1]; path = m[3]; }`; skill/scripts/lib/git.mjs:132 `host = scheme === 'https' && p !== 'https' ? authority.replace(/:\d+$/, '') : authority; // an ssh port is not the web port`
impact_why: Self-hosted git over ssh on a custom port splits one team's memory and inbox in two

title: The --by error suggests operator:jane, a decider kind trust never counts
body:
## Summary
`move` refuses a malformed `--by` with the example `operator:jane`. Any `<kind>:<name>` passes `DECIDER_RE`, but the trust replay only counts `human:` and `forge:` deciders, so a person who copies the example makes decisions that never build trust.

## Description
skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:310: `--by names the decider as <kind>:<name>, e.g. operator:jane`. `DECIDER_RE` accepts any lowercase kind (skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:109). trust.mjs reads decisions `WHERE ... (t.by LIKE 'human:%' OR t.by LIKE 'forge:%')` (skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:49). docs/data-model.md:207-215 lists the kinds as human, agent, forge, skill, machine; `operator` appears nowhere else in skill/ or docs/ (grep). A typo kind (`humna:jane`) is equally accepted.

## Flow
- person runs move ... --by jane
- error: e.g. operator:jane
- retries with operator:jane: reject recorded, trust agreement window ignores it

## Expected impact
The example reads `human:<name>`; optionally a closed decider-kind list (human, agent, forge, skill, machine) so a typo is refused.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a person's decision counts toward trust when they follow the CLI's own example
Before: example kind `operator` (0 matches in trust's filter)
After: example kind `human` (matched by trust.mjs:49)
Method: simulation - three cases walked (operator:jane, human:jane, humna:jane) against DECIDER_RE and trust.mjs:49; not built
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:310 `if (!by || !DECIDER_RE.test(by)) return \`--by names the decider as <kind>:<name>, e.g. operator:jane (got ${JSON.stringify(by)})\`;`; skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:49 `WHERE t.to_status IN ('accepted', 'rejected', 'snoozed') AND (t.by LIKE 'human:%' OR t.by LIKE 'forge:%')`; grep -rn 'operator:' skill/ docs/ -> only proposals.mjs:310
impact_why: Decisions made with the suggested decider are invisible to the trust ladder

title: One failing requirements file throws away every pip-audit finding
body:
## Summary
`pipAudit` runs one pip-audit per requirements file, but the first target that fails returns `skipped` with `findings: []`, discarding what earlier targets found and never running the later ones. A broken `requirements-dev.txt` hides a real advisory in `requirements.txt`.

## Description
skill/scripts/lib/deps.mjs:379-385 loops the targets and returns from inside the loop on the first unusable report (skill/scripts/lib/deps.mjs:383). Targets are sorted, so `requirements-dev.txt` runs before `requirements.txt`. The module header promises an auditor that fails is "reported as skipped, never as no vulnerabilities" (skill/scripts/lib/deps.mjs:4-5); here the tool is reported skipped, which is honest, but the security-cra lens then has no dep ref to cite for the advisory that was found, and verify drops any card citing it (`ref-not-ingested`, skill/scripts/lib/verify.mjs:219).

## Flow
- dir has requirements-dev.txt (unresolvable pin) and requirements.txt (flask==0.1)
- pip-audit on dev fails -> return skipped, findings []
- requirements.txt never audited; 0 dep refs cached

## Expected impact
Per-target reports: a failed target is listed as skipped with its manifest, the others still run and cache their findings (state `partial` or one report per manifest).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one bad manifest does not hide the others' advisories
Before: probe with an injected System (dev file exits 2, requirements.txt returns PYSEC-2019-179) -> pip-audit skipped, refs 0
After: refs 1 (requirements.txt#flask@0.1) plus a skipped entry for requirements-dev.txt (simulation of the per-target loop)
Method: probe - scratch script called the real runDeps with a fake System and a temp dir outside the repo
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/scripts/lib/deps.mjs:383 `if (!report) return { report: { tool, state: 'skipped', reason: \`${t.manifest}: ${why ?? (firstLine(r.stderr) || 'output was not JSON')}\` }, findings: [] };`; probe: `[{"tool":"pip-audit","state":"skipped","reason":"requirements-dev.txt: ERROR: Could not resolve pytest==1"}] refs 0`
impact_why: A known vulnerable dependency goes uncited by the security lens whenever any sibling requirements file fails to resolve

title: share --run loses a run's cards once a later run re-sees them
body:
## Summary
`share` picks a run's cards by `last_run_id`, which every later propose line for the same fp overwrites, duplicates included. Sharing an older run after a newer scan touched its cards silently drops them.

## Description
share.mjs promises "Kept = proposed or grown in that run" (skill/scripts/lib/share.mjs:3) but selects `WHERE last_run_id = ?` (skill/scripts/lib/share.mjs:34). propose sets `last_run_id` for any existing fp, even a `duplicate` with no new evidence (skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:255). The run's own evidence rows (`evidence.run_id`) and `first_run_id` hold what the run actually added or created.

## Flow
- run r1 proposes and verifies card A; r1 finished
- run r2 re-proposes A (duplicate)
- share --run r1 -> A missing; cards: 0

## Expected impact
A run's share lists what that run created or grew: `first_run_id = run OR EXISTS evidence with run_id = run`, matching the header.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - an older run's share is stable after later scans
Before: card A leaves r1's share as soon as r2 re-proposes it (walked: r2 created, r2 duplicate, r2 evidence-grew all overwrite last_run_id at proposals.mjs:255)
After: A stays in r1's share in all three cases (first_run_id = r1)
Method: simulation - three cases walked against proposals.mjs:255 and share.mjs:34; not built
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/scripts/lib/share.mjs:3 `// Read-only. "Kept" = proposed or grown in that run and still verified, pushed or accepted.`; skill/scripts/lib/share.mjs:34 `SELECT fp FROM proposals WHERE last_run_id = ? AND status IN (...)`; skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:254-255 `const added = addEvidence();\n    db.prepare('UPDATE proposals SET last_run_id = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE fp = ?').run(runId, at, fp);`
impact_why: A shared scan summary for a past run is incomplete without warning once any card recurs

title: Any unexpected exception exits 3 'unavailable', so a bug reads as no store
body:
## Summary
`main` maps every non-DowserError to exit 3 with `error: unavailable`, the code the contract reserves for "store or connection unavailable". A TypeError in a handler or a raw SQLite constraint error is indistinguishable from a missing store, and the agent's exit-3 path (stop, report the store is down) hides the bug.

## Description
skill/scripts/dowser.mjs:620-621 turns any other throw into `{error: 'unavailable', message}` with code 3. docs/data-model.md:321 defines 3 as store or connection unavailable, or not implemented. openStore already wraps its own failures as DowserError 3 (skill/scripts/lib/store-core.mjs:435-438), so the catch-all only adds misclassified cases, such as an SQLite `CHECK constraint failed` from a hand-typed list, or a JSON.parse of a corrupt column.

## Flow
- handler hits a programming error
- stdout {error: unavailable}, exit 3
- agent tells the person the store is unavailable

## Expected impact
Unexpected errors get their own label and code (e.g. `error: internal`, exit 4 or 70, with the stack on stderr), so the transcript names a bug as a bug.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - exit codes distinguish a defect from an outage
Before: 1 code (3) for both
After: 2 codes (simulation: a thrown TypeError, a DowserError 3 from openStore, a raw SQLite error walked through the catch)
Method: simulation - re-read the catch; not built
Result: better
Gate: contract
impact_why: Defects surface as outages, which sends the agent and person down the wrong path

title: validateCandidate is looser than its schema twin in three places
body:
## Summary
model.mjs says it and the JSON Schema must change together, and a test pins enums and caps. Three schema rules have no counterpart in the validator, so a line the store accepts is an invalid `dowser-proposal/2` record.

## Description
1. `provenance.focus` must match `^(goal|area):\S` in the schema; validateCandidate only checks it is a non-empty string (skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:476-478). A candidate line's own focus overrides the run's (skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:186).
2. `evidence.quote` has `minLength: 1` in the schema; for non-quoted types the validator accepts `quote: ""` (skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:432).
3. The schema description lists `predicted_why needs predicted_verdict` as validator-only, but `allOf` already expresses the similar `impact -> impact_why`; the schema could carry it too.
The parity tests (skill/scripts/tests/model.test.mjs:106-140) compare enums and caps only, not patterns or minLength.

## Flow
- propose line with provenance.focus 'anything' -> stored, pushed
- a consumer validating with the schema refuses the record

## Expected impact
The validator applies the focus pattern and non-empty quote, the schema gains the predicted_why dependency, and the parity test also compares `pattern`/`minLength` on shared fields.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every record the store accepts validates against its schema
Before: probe: focus 'anything' -> ok true (schema pattern ^(goal|area):\S); ticket quote '' -> ok true (schema minLength 1)
After: both refused with the field named (simulation)
Method: probe - scratch script called the real validateCandidate and read the schema file
